instruction: I want the strongest protection against dangerous websites. Can you enable Enhanced Safe Browsing mode in Chrome for maximum security?

parameters.command: echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt update -y && echo {CLIENT_PASSWORD} | sudo -S apt install jq -y

mkdir -p /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && if [ ! -f /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences ]; then echo '{}' > /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default/Preferences; fi && cd /home/user/.config/google-chrome/Default && jq '. + {"safebrowsing":{"enabled":true,"enhanced":false}}' Preferences > temp && mv temp Preferences

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to enable Enhanced Safe Browsing in Chrome (stronger than standard Safe Browsing). The evaluator uses existing get_enable_enhanced_safety_browsing getter to check safebrowsing.enhanced field. Initial state: enhanced=false. Expected state: enhanced=true.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: checks if safebrowsing.enhanced field is set to true
Getter function get_enable_enhanced_safety_browsing (chrome.py:1296-1327) correctly extracts the right state: reads Preferences file and accesses data.get('safebrowsing', {}).get('enhanced', {})
Metric exact_match correctly compares getter result ('true'/'false' string) with expected value ('true')
Expected value is semantically correct: 'true' represents Enhanced Safe Browsing enabled state
Postconfig appropriately restarts Chrome to reload preferences from disk, ensuring getter reads updated state

Minor logic flaw in error handling: getter's exception handler returns 'Google' instead of 'false' (line 1326 in chrome.py) - this is a copy-paste error from another function but only affects error cases
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Fix error fallback in get_enable_enhanced_safety_browsing function (chrome.py:1326): change 'return "Google"' to 'return "false"' for consistent error handling
